prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro CBTC (peak/off-peak/engineering hours). Degraded: LTC declares when MA, localization, point detection, platform interface or radio untrusted (=loss of comms); trains stationary/controlled speed until separation restored; controller action before auto departure. Triage: safety critical, service affecting, cyber, maintenance-only. Return to auto: stable comms, verified route, confirmed position, recorded handback; cyber controls prerequisite. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC, OCC; holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through via Lantern; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; receives Route Release Exception List; non-vital; manual route recovery; concurs with Maple on resets; notified of cyber events needing auto restriction or comms-mode change). Revenue Train Operator (acknowledgements to Atlas; repeats back limit/speed/stop/platform-clear; restricted manual speed/stopping/doors; sends Test Train Clearance Memo to Lantern; no cyber admin in service). Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (verifies points/vacancy/protection; Axle Counter Reset Request; remote read-only outside window; access needs CSO approval). Cyber Security Officer (monitors Safety Data Communication Network, Saffron, Lantern; correlates auth failures, resets, rejected messages, config changes, timing without touching safety paths; uses audit file; approves sensitive permissions). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; never obscures alarms; needs Test Train Clearance Memo before non-revenue security exceptions). Service Timetable Server. Passenger Information Gateway. Voice Dispatch Console (authorizes restricted manual moves). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction; applies TSR Notice); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction); both send MA. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (sends Axle Counter Reset Request; rejects invalid signature/expired certificate/out-of-window sequence). West Junction Interlocking (sends Route Release Exception List). Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel (restricted manual if no MA; Brake Curve Checksum Log). Dual Channel Odometer. Train Radio Modem (reports safe-data loss to Atlas). Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron. Maintenance Diagnostic Server (can't alter MA or bypass certificates). Quarry (alias, unnamed; tags sessions with incident ID). Platform Screen Door Controller. Document units:
S218: Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.
S219: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
S220: The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
S221: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
S222: The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.
S223: Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
S224: Commissioning shall begin only after the installed equipment baseline for the Atlas Onboard Controller, Dual Channel Odometer, Train Radio Modem, and wayside control equipment has been configuration checked against the approved release record.
S225: The test-train phase shall use non-passenger movements to prove train localization, movement authority processing, braking response, radio continuity, and operator displays under controlled operating conditions.
S226: Each test train shall be crewed by a Revenue Train Operator qualified for commissioning duties and supported by a Line Traffic Controller with authority to stop the trial when observed conditions depart from the approved script.
S227: Initial movements shall be conducted at restricted commissioning speeds and shall progress to representative service speeds only after the Atlas Onboard Controller and North District Zone Controller demonstrate stable supervision.
S228: The South District Zone Controller shall be commissioned under the same test regime so that boundary behavior is verified before whole-line operation is attempted.
S229: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking shall remain under enhanced monitoring during migration because route setting, point detection, and authority release behavior are critical to mixed-mode operation.
S230: The staged migration from legacy signalling shall divide the railway into controlled areas that can be commissioned, operated, and, if necessary, returned to legacy control without affecting uncommissioned areas.
S231: Cutover planning shall define the exact control boundaries, permissible train movements, staffing levels, and rollback conditions for each migration stage.
S232: Before any cutover stage, the Safety Data Communication Network and Wayside Radio Access Network shall be verified for coverage, latency, redundancy, and alarm presentation at the control center.
